scope: Independent source and statement review of Lemma C.2 only. Lean elaboration, dependency identity, and transitive axiom audit are separate recorded checks. This review makes no claim for the other paper results.

review: Option (Bool × Fin p) retains the zero point and two original signed labels per coordinate; cardinality is exactly 2p+1.
Both one-sided and absolute signed maxima equal the actual infinity norm.

The discrete metric tests equality of the original labels. The standard-deviation metric is identified with the finite Euclidean canonical pseudometric, giving diagonal, symmetry, and triangle properties without a rank assumption.
Actual observation contrasts are measurable, centered, and independent, with first and second integrability derived from the original bounded envelope.
The envelope is 2δ off the diagonal and zero on it; actual summed contrast variances equal the covariance quadratic form.

The archive scalar MGF is instantiated, rather than assumed. The explicit Laplace parameter q/(s+bq) permits s=0; the b=0 case is separately proved. Applying the bound to both signs gives mixed-tail scales 4d1 and 2d2.
The finite-net equality matches admissible nonempty subsets and a singleton first level. Nonemptiness makes the printed distance to a subset meaningful.
The real Gaussian weight 2^(k/2) is proved equal to sqrt(2)^k; exponential weight is exactly 2^k.
Homogeneity records both actual Bernstein factors. The functional is finite for the actual finite canonical metric; the discrete cutoff upper bound is finite.
Dirksen is applied to actual signed increments at the zero base point with proved integrability and the C2.2 mixed tail.
Unit covariance diagonal and actual zero coordinate means give second moment one; Cauchy--Schwarz (via nonnegative variance of |X|) bounds every signed first absolute moment by one.
The resulting bound has coefficients 96 for gamma2, 192 for gamma1, and additive term2. No desired maximum comparison occurs among the raw-data premises.
Nat.clog2 (Nat.clog2 m) is proved the least cutoff satisfying m≤2^(2^k). Since p≥1, m=2p+1≥3 and this cutoff is positive, retaining a singleton at level0.

The explicit paper-facing witness uses singleton {none} before the cutoff and all original labels thereafter. The functional bound uses the library proof of this same singleton/full construction, whose initial representative may be arbitrary because the metric is discrete.
The finite geometric sum is bounded by 4log(2p+1), and log(2p+1)≤2log(ep), yielding 8δL. All inequalities include p=1.
A factor of the actual covariance exists from bounded-independent data, including singular covariance; the actual Gaussian law is supported on that factor range.

Signed factor rows reproduce actual contrast second moments and canonical distances. The one-sided signed width equals the Gaussian infinity-norm expectation, so the checked lower majorizing-measure direction applies directly.

Zero canonical distance forces almost-sure equality of actual signed Gaussian coordinates. Passing to the surjective finite image preserves gamma2, the almost-sure Gaussian maximum, and its width. These quotient operations do not occur in the discrete metric or its bound.
The unit Gaussian marginal has exact absolute first moment sqrt(2/pi); domination by the infinity norm gives the lower bound including p=1.
The final constant max(96*gaussianMajorizingConstant+2/sqrt(2/pi),1536) is fixed before probability space, dimensions, observations, envelope, and factor.

The raw theorem derives nonnegative δ from the original boundedness assumptions with n≥1. Its only probabilistic inputs are measurable centered independent bounded observations and actual unit summed marginal variances; an actual covariance factor identifies gΣ and is separately proved to exist.
